group.passage: Do you set up notifications on your smartphone to remind you to keep up with the latest news feeds or the most recent updates that your friends post on the social media, fearing that you are not always a member of those who are in the know? If you do, you are a victim of FOMO. FOMO is an acronym meaning “fear of missing out.” It refers to a compulsory need, often in the form of anxiety, to be socially connected with a group. Social media, which facilitates people’s reliance on technology for connection, is primarily, but not exclusively, the breeding ground of this phenomenon. Once missing out some status updates, the FOMO crowd may suffer from feelings of isolation and self-doubt, followed by physical problems such as fatigue, stress, or sleep disorders. FOMO can also be an obstacle to personal success, because the preoccupation with what others are doing will hold back people from making progress in real life. On the other hand, JOMO, or “joy of missing out,” is the mindful practice of drawing boundaries within a social group to break away from the real or virtual connections. The core of JOMO is to make a conscious effort to disengage from relationships, to look within instead of without, and to find existential meanings in ourselves. People can foster the JOMO state-of-mind by staying in pajamas throughout a day, reading a favorite novel repeatedly, or going out for a walk without any destination in mind. Missing out can be joyful, because people can be given some breathing space to savor life. It is human nature to be tribal, but attending an activity simply out of the fear of missing out is not fulfilling. If you would like to turn from FOMO to JOMO, you can try to disconnect yourself from technology for the time being!
